title: Forbidding a carried bolt stack did not immediately change ammunition choice
claim: During one fight, a marksman carried both wooden bolts and 25 copper bolts. Temporarily setting the carried wooden stack's forbid flag did not immediately switch his shots to copper: the wooden count fell from ten to two while the copper count stayed at 25. The flag was restored afterward.
reproduction: On a disposable backed-up encounter, record the exact carried stacks, their materials and flags, projectile reports and quantities before and after a short interval. Separate a selection preference, a loaded projectile and actual ammunition fired.
evidence: Firsthand AI-assisted Namemerchants observations on 2026-11-02; sanitized summaries of native state, not a published save or raw telemetry.
While the wooden stack was forbidden, native reports still described glumprong bolts striking the undead.
A wooden bolt report described damage to a thrips brain; an attacker died. Copper consumption was observed later.
limitations: One live fortress on Windows; relevant mods were not fully inventoried. Community reproduction is pending. This is a negative result from one held-stack experiment, not a universal ammunition algorithm or a recommended combat procedure. Preloaded shots or assignment behavior were not fully separated.
